title: Cost-Efficient, High-Precision Enterprise AI with Everpure Data Stream
summary: Learn how Everpure Data Stream delivers high-precision enterprise AI at sustainable cost, pairing efficient open models with retrieval on your own data.
body_markdown:
### Summary


Everpure Data Stream pairs NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano and retrieval over your own data to deliver grounded, cited answers at a fraction of frontier-model cost and energy—with data that never leaves your data center.


Ask anyone who has taken an AI pilot into production what surprised them most, and you’ll rarely hear about accuracy. You’ll hear about the bill. A copilot that delighted a hundred users becomes a budget line nobody approved at ten thousand. The model didn’t get worse. The meter just kept running.


That’s because the economics of enterprise AI are driven by token volume, and token volume grows faster than anyone plans for. Agents that reason through dozens of steps, documents that run to hundreds of pages, images that get analyzed again and again—each one multiplies the number of tokens flowing through your models. If every one of those tokens is priced at frontier-API rates, cost scales faster than value.


[Everpure Data Stream](https://www.pure.ai/data-stream.html) was built on a different premise: that an enterprise should be able to hold answer quality high while the cost of each answer keeps falling. Here’s how it does that—and why the choice of model at its heart matters so much.


## What is Everpure Data Stream?


Everpure Data Stream brings AI capabilities directly to enterprise data where it already lives, replacing manual data ingestion and preparation with a GPU-accelerated pipeline that runs from ingestion to inference—making unstructured data AI-ready for retrieval, inference, and generative use cases. It’s the core of Everpure’s strategy to deliver AI-ready data. Built on the NVIDIA AI Data Platform reference design, it was[introduced in beta at NVIDIA GTC 2026](https://www.storagenewsletter.com/2026/03/18/nvidia-gtc-2026-everpure-simplifies-enterprise-ai-with-evergreen-one-for-ai-and-data-stream-beta/) and[announced for general availability at Pure Accelerate](https://www.storagenewsletter.com/2026/06/26/pure-accelerate-2026-everpure-announces-data-stream-to-expand-ai-ready-data-offerings/) , where Everpure described it as cutting raw data preparation from months to minutes while keeping information inside the corporate network. (Our[launch blog](https://blog.everpuredata.com/products/driving-the-future-of-ai-data-readiness-pure-storage-data-stream/) and[NVIDIA’s announcement of this new infrastructure class](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-storage-industry-leaders-unveil-new-class-of-enterprise-infrastructure-for-the-age-of-ai) tell the fuller story.)


At its core, the platform combines:


- NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano—an open mixture-of-experts language model that carries roughly 31.6 billion parameters of knowledge but activates only about 3.6 billion per token, so it runs on a single enterprise GPU with context support up to one million tokens
- NVIDIA retrieval models—dedicated embedding models for text and images, plus a reranker, each small and purpose-built for its one job in the pipeline
- Everpure™[FlashBlade//S](https://www.everpuredata.com/content/dam/pdf/en/datasheets/ds-pure-storage-flashblade-s.pdf) ™—the unified fast file and object platform that holds the source data, the vector indexes, and everything in between


Every question your teams ask runs against data that has already been ingested, classified, embedded, and indexed—with access controls enforced and citations attached. That architecture, it turns out, is also where the savings live.


## Why token volume is the hidden bill in enterprise AI


Most AI cost conversations start with GPUs. But the teams who have run agents in production know the real meter is tokens—and agents are voracious. An agent doesn’t answer once; it plans, retrieves, calls tools, checks its work, and iterates, re-sending its accumulated context at every step. A task that looks like one question is often 30 model calls, and a long-running session can be hundreds.


Frontier models like[OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) and[Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) list at roughly $3 to $5 per million input tokens and $15 to $30 per million output tokens. Nemotron 3 Nano is[publicly hosted](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b) at $0.05 and $0.20. Running inside Everpure Data Stream on GPUs you already own, the marginal cost of one more agent step is closer to the electricity than to either number. When the same intelligence gets called 500 times a day, that gap is the whole story.


> A long-running agent quietly becomes one of the most expensive employees in the building—unless the model it calls is priced for being called.


## A small model with big-model precision


The instinct to reach for the largest model available is understandable, and for the everyday work of the enterprise, it’s usually wrong. NVIDIA’s published results show Nemotron 3 Nano delivering up to 3.3 times the inference throughput of similarly sized open models while scoring higher on popular benchmarks—and using up to 60% fewer reasoning tokens to reach an answer than its predecessor. In an agentic system, that efficiency pays twice: each token costs less, and fewer tokens are needed in the first place.


Precision, meanwhile, comes less from model size than from what the model gets to read. A frontier model with no access to your corpus produces fluent, confident, wrong answers. Everpure Data Stream retrieves first and generates second: hybrid semantic, keyword, and relationship search narrows millions of documents to the right few passages, a reranker orders them, and the model reasons over evidence rather than guessing. Right-sized model, right context, cited answer. That combination is what lets cost fall without accuracy falling with it.


There’s an energy story here too, and it’s not a footnote. Activating 3.6 billion parameters per token instead of hundreds of billions is an order-of-magnitude difference in compute per answer. As AI shifts from experiment to utility, watts per answer becomes a number boards ask about—and it’s one of the few that can trend down while usage trends up.


## Input is free, and output costs pennies on the frontier dollar


The pattern that quietly ruins AI budgets is re-reading. Stuff a filing into a model’s context window per question, and you pay to process the whole document every single time. Everpure Data Stream inverts that: the heavy work of reading your estate—extraction, OCR, chunking, embedding—happens once, on your GPUs, as a batch job. After that, each question retrieves a few thousand tokens of relevant evidence instead of a few hundred thousand tokens of raw document. That is the economic payoff of data readiness: prepare the data once, and every answer afterward gets cheaper. Across the workloads we see most, that’s where the largest savings sit. Use case examples include:


- **Financial services:** A single annual report can exceed 200,000 tokens; credit files and deal rooms run to millions. Retrieval-first answers routinely cut input tokens per query by 50 to 100 times—before any per-token price difference is counted.
- **Healthcare:** Hospital systems hold millions of images paired with reports and notes. Vision APIs re-tokenize and re-bill an image on every question, and the data leaves the building each time. Everpure Data Stream embeds each image once with a multimodal model; the thousandth query against the index costs about the same as the first, and protected health information never leaves the data center.
- **Agentic operations:** Long-running agents with big working contexts hit both problems at once—many calls, large inputs. A million tokens of context support, cheap tokens, and efficient reasoning keep multi-hour sessions affordable.

## Built for the enterprise—not just the demo


Cost efficiency isn’t sustainable if someone else can reprice it, and precision isn’t trustworthy if you can’t govern it. Everpure Data Stream treats both as platform properties:


- **Your model, on your schedule:** NVIDIA Nemotron is an open model. Pin the version you validated, fine-tune it on your domain, and upgrade when you decide to—no silent updates or deprecation deadlines reaching into production workflows.
- **Sovereignty by architecture:** Prompts, documents, and answers stay in your data center because there’s no external call to make—a design fact, not a contract clause.
- **Governed answers:** Access controls follow the user, so people only see answers drawn from documents they’re entitled to read, with citations back to the source.
- **Predictable spend:** Fixed, owned infrastructure means the cost curve flattens as usage grows, instead of accelerating with it.


## Where frontier models still earn their keep


None of this argues that frontier models are obsolete. Genuinely open-ended reasoning—novel synthesis, unconstrained planning, frontier-grade code generation—still belongs on frontier systems, and Everpure Data Stream doesn’t prevent you from routing the occasional hard case there deliberately. What it prevents is paying frontier prices, frontier energy, and frontier data exposure for the large majority of enterprise work that a well-grounded, efficient model handles correctly at a fraction of the cost.


## Precision you can afford to scale


High accuracy and low cost are usually framed as a tradeoff. In practice, they’re the same engineering problem: read your data once, retrieve precisely, generate efficiently, and keep the whole loop under your control. It’s the same premise behind everything Everpure builds for AI: there’s no AI strategy without a data-readiness strategy. Everpure Data Stream makes those choices in the architecture, so the economics still work on the day your pilot becomes everyone’s daily tool.
